# Gobbly.io: every question and answer

Source: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/  (updated 2026-11-17)

## What is Gobbly.io?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/what-is-it/

Gobbly.io is a free casual game for iPhone and Android where you roll a hungry little ball around colourful maps, eat the goal items before the timer runs out, and grow bigger with every bite. You start each level as a small ball that can only eat little things, and every bite helps you grow until you can eat cakes, chairs and cars. It is free on the App Store and Google Play. What do you actually do in the game? The game is made of levels. Each level shows a few goal cards at the top, such as 120 cookies, 30 donuts and 4 burgers. Eat every goal item before the timer reaches zero and you win the level. There are hundreds of levels, with HARD and SUPER HARD levels along the way. The ball starts every level at Size 1. Everything you eat fills the ring around it, and when the ring is full the ball grows to the next size and can eat bigger things. What kind of game is it? Eat-and-grow game: the same idea as hole games and the classic rolling-ball games: get bigger by swallowing what is around you. Level game: hundreds of short levels, each with its own goal list and timer, that get trickier in waves. Casual game: one finger, learned in seconds, a level fits into a short break. Why a ball instead of a hole? A hole sits flat on the ground and things drop into it. A ball rolls through the world, bumps into things and grows bigger on screen. Tall piles of food slide down into it as you eat the bottom, which makes eating feel physical. What else is in the game? Boosters help when a level is tight: Bigger Ball, Magnet, Shield, Compass, Freeze, Rainbow Potion and Clock. You earn them as rewards and can buy them with coins. Winning levels earns coins and stars. On top of the levels there are daily gifts, a prize road, win-streak gifts, the Super Star power, Critter Hunts, a Weekly Contest, a monthly Season Pass, a card album and a collection book of everything you have eaten. Who made it? Gobbly.io is made by Sultan of Niyyat, an independent developer. It is not made by, or connected to, the companies behind Hole.io, Katamari Damacy or other games in the genre. Where can you get it? Only from the official stores: Gobbly.io on the App Store and Gobbly.io on Google Play .

## How do you play Gobbly.io?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-to-play/

Touch anywhere on the screen and drag: the ball rolls the way you drag. Lift your finger and it stops. Roll into food and things that are small enough and the ball eats them. Eat every item on the goal cards before the timer runs out to win the level. How do the controls work? Touch anywhere on the screen and drag: the ball rolls the way you drag. Lift your finger and it stops. There are no buttons to learn in the play area, only the booster bar at the bottom and the pause button. What are the goal cards? The cards under the timer show what you must eat and how many are left. Each one counts down as you eat. When every card is done, the level is won at once, and seconds left on the clock give you a small coin bonus. How do you grow? The ball starts every level at Size 1. Everything you eat fills the ring around it, and when the ring is full the ball grows to the next size and can eat bigger things. Small things are worth a little, bigger things are worth more. A "Size" label under the ball shows how big you are. What happens if the time runs out? An "OUT OF TIME" screen shows what you still had to eat. You can buy 20 more seconds with coins, watch a short video for more time, or give up. Giving up costs one heart. What are bombs and hearts? Some maps have bombs. If the ball eats a bomb, the level ends, unless a Shield is protecting you. You can then pay coins to carry on, or give up. You have 5 hearts. Losing a level costs one heart, and one heart comes back every 30 minutes. You can also refill them with coins, or watch a short video for one heart. What are boosters? Boosters help when a level is tight: Bigger Ball, Magnet, Shield, Compass, Freeze, Rainbow Potion and Clock. You earn them as rewards and can buy them with coins. Is it hard to learn? No. The first level teaches itself without any text. Getting good is about choosing a route: eat the small things first, grow, then go for the big goal items.

## Is Gobbly.io like Hole.io?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-is-it-different-from-hole-io/

It is the same family of game: you swallow things, grow bigger and can then swallow bigger things. The differences are that in Gobbly.io you are a rolling ball, not a hole, and you play single-player levels with a goal list and a timer instead of racing other players to be the biggest. What is the same? You start small and grow by eating things. The bigger you are, the bigger the things you can eat. There is a timer, and one finger controls everything. What is different? Hole.io Gobbly.io You are A hole in the ground A ball rolling through the world Goal Be the biggest when the timer ends Eat everything on the level's goal list before the timer ends Other players Other holes in the same city None: single-player levels Progress Separate rounds Hundreds of levels, boosters, events and a Season Pass Is it a copy of Hole.io? No. Hole.io made the hole version of this idea popular on phones, and the rolling-ball idea goes back to Katamari Damacy on PlayStation 2 in 2004. Gobbly.io is an independent game by Sultan of Niyyat with its own maps, food and levels, and it is not connected to either. If I like Hole.io, will I like this? Very likely, if what you enjoy is the growing and the moment you are finally big enough for the big things. If you mainly enjoy beating other players, note that Gobbly.io is about beating the clock instead.

## What can the ball eat, and why can't I eat that yet?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/what-can-the-ball-absorb/

The ball can eat anything whose size is the same as the ball's size or smaller. If something will not go in, the ball is not big enough yet: eat smaller things nearby, grow a size, and come back. How does the size rule work? Every item belongs to a size, from Size 1 (cherries, cookies, small sweets) up to the biggest things on the map. The ball starts every level at Size 1. Everything you eat fills the ring around it, and when the ring is full the ball grows to the next size and can eat bigger things. Things that are too big for you act like walls: the ball slides along them. How do I know when I can eat something new? When the ball grows, the game shows which new things you can now eat. On early levels a small red ring also flashes when you bump into something that is still too big. What are the piles and stacks? Many levels have tall stacks and big heaps of food. The ball eats them from the bottom and the rest slides down into it, so a whole pile pours in while you hold still next to it. What should I never eat? Bombs. Some maps have bombs. If the ball eats a bomb, the level ends, unless a Shield is protecting you. You can then pay coins to carry on, or give up. Why did my ball stop growing? Usually because the things around you are already eaten, or still too big. Head for an area full of food you can eat. The Compass booster points you to the goal items you still need.

## How do you grow faster in Gobbly.io?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-to-grow-faster/

Eat as many small things as you can in the first seconds, roll through crowded areas instead of chasing single items, and move up to bigger things as soon as you grow. Keep moving: empty ground wastes time. What are the best tips to grow fast? Go for crowds. A line or pile of small food is worth more than single items spread across the map. Keep rolling. The ball eats as it rolls past. Rolling through a full area beats stopping on one item. Park next to piles. Tall stacks pour into the ball by themselves while you sit at their base. Move up a size as soon as you can. Bigger things fill the size ring much faster. Do not go back to cleared ground. Head for places you have not been. Use Magnet when food is spread out. It pulls things in from farther away. Start with Bigger Ball or Rainbow Potion on hard levels. Rainbow Potion starts you at Size 2. Watch out for bombs. One wrong bite ends the level, so slow down near them or use a Shield. Is it better to eat small or big things? Both, at the right time. Small things early, because they are all you can eat. Big things as soon as you can, because each one is worth much more. The mistake is staying on small things after you have outgrown them.

## How do you beat a hard level in Gobbly.io?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-to-beat-a-level/

Read the goal cards first, grow quickly on the small food, and only then go for the big goal items that need a high size. Use boosters on HARD and SUPER HARD levels, and keep away from bombs. Every level can be beaten without buying anything. How should I read the goal cards? Most levels mix "many small" goals (lots of cookies), "some medium" goals and "a few big" goals that you can only eat after growing. Eat the small goal items as you grow, and save the big ones for when you are big enough. Which boosters help most? Clock and Freeze: more time, or the timer stops for a while. Magnet: pulls food in from farther away. Compass: points to the goal items you still need. Shield: protects you from a bomb. Bigger Ball and Rainbow Potion: a head start on size. What do I do when time is nearly out? Go straight for the goal items that are closest. When the cards with only a few items left start to pulse, that is the game telling you what is left. If time runs out, you can buy 20 more seconds with coins or watch a video for more time. What are HARD and SUPER HARD levels? Every few levels the game gets tougher for one level, with a tighter clock or more to eat. They give bigger rewards. This is a good moment to use the boosters you have saved.

## What are the most common beginner mistakes?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/beginner-mistakes/

The big ones are going for the big goal items before you are big enough, stopping on single items, going back over cleared ground, and rolling into bombs. Fix those and levels get much easier. Which mistakes do new players make most? Going for big goals too early. You bounce off and lose time. Fix: grow on small food first. Stopping on single items. Fix: roll through crowds of food. Going back over cleared ground. Fix: always head for places you have not been. Rolling into bombs. Fix: slow down near them, or use a Shield. Saving boosters forever. Fix: use them on HARD levels; you earn more as rewards. Giving up too fast. Giving up costs a heart. Fix: if you were close, take the extra time. How long does it take to get good? Not long. The first levels teach the basics, and most players get the hang of routes and sizes within a few levels.

## Who should play Gobbly.io?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/who-should-play/

Gobbly.io suits people who want a quick, easy, satisfying game: fans of Hole.io and other eat-and-grow games, people who play in short breaks, and anyone who likes clearing a full map. It is not for players looking for a story, deep strategy or live matches against other people. Who will enjoy it most? Fans of eat-and-grow games. If you liked hole games or Katamari, the loop will feel familiar. People who like satisfying games. Piles pouring into the ball scratches the same itch as clean-up games. Short-break players. A level takes about 1 to 3 minutes. People who like collecting. Winning levels earns coins and stars. On top of the levels there are daily gifts, a prize road, win-streak gifts, the Super Star power, Critter Hunts, a Weekly Contest, a monthly Season Pass, a card album and a collection book of everything you have eaten. Who will probably not enjoy it? Players who want a story or characters to follow. People looking for deep strategy or building. Players who want live matches against other people. Gobbly.io is a single-player game. There are no other balls in a level and no live opponents. The Weekly Contest and rankings are worked out on your phone, and there is no chat. Anyone who dislikes ads in free games. There are optional reward videos you can choose to watch for extras such as more time, a heart or coins. From level 4, a short full-screen ad can also appear now and then between levels and when you come back to the game. Do I need to be good at games? No. Drag your finger and the ball follows. The early levels are easy, and the harder ones come slowly.

## Why are games like Gobbly.io so satisfying?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-satisfying/

Eat-and-grow games give you constant small rewards: every bite makes you visibly bigger, and a crowded map slowly becomes clean. Gobbly.io adds piles of food that pour into the ball and a goal list that ticks down, so there is always a "just a few left" moment. What makes these games feel so good? Constant progress. Every bite fills the size ring. Clearing a mess. A full map turning into empty ground is like tidying a room. Power growth. Things that blocked you a minute ago are now food. A clear finish. The last goal item going in with seconds left. What makes the ball version special? Tall stacks and heaps slide down into the ball as it eats their base, with little "+1" pops, sounds and vibration. Watching a whole pile pour in is the moment people come back for. Is it like ASMR games? It shares the calm, repetitive and pleasing side: lots of small pickups and a tidy result. It is more active, because you steer the whole time and there is a clock.

## Is Gobbly.io a relaxing game?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-good-for-relaxing/

Mostly, yes. The controls are simple, levels are short and there is no one else to fight, so it is easy to switch off and just roll around eating things. The timer adds a little tension, and harder levels ask for more focus. Why do people find it relaxing? No story to follow and no other players. Your hands do one simple thing. Clearing a map is a tidy, finished feeling. Levels take about 1 to 3 minutes, so it is easy to stop. Is it stressful at all? A little, in a light way: the clock counts down, and bombs on some maps end the level. You have 5 hearts. Losing a level costs one heart, and one heart comes back every 30 minutes. You can also refill them with coins, or watch a short video for one heart. Will ads interrupt the calm? There are optional reward videos you can choose to watch for extras such as more time, a heart or coins. From level 4, a short full-screen ad can also appear now and then between levels and when you come back to the game. Tap REMOVE ADS on the ad break screen. It is a one-time purchase that switches off the ads between levels and when you open the game, for good. Buying anything else in the game switches them off too. Reward videos you choose to watch stay available.

## Is Gobbly.io suitable for kids?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-ok-for-kids/

The game itself is simple and non-violent: a ball rolls around eating food and toys. It is rated 4+ on the App Store; the game is meant for players aged 13 and over. Parents should know about ads and purchases: There are optional reward videos you can choose to watch for extras such as more time, a heart or coins. From level 4, a short full-screen ad can also appear now and then between levels and when you come back to the game. Optional purchases are coin packs, booster bundles, a Gold Season Pass and a one-time Remove Ads. Every level can be beaten without buying anything. Is there violence or scary content? No. Food and toys disappear into the ball. Bombs give a cartoon "BOOM" and end the level; nothing is hurt. Can kids talk to strangers in the game? No. There is no chat and no messaging. Gobbly.io is a single-player game. There are no other balls in a level and no live opponents. The Weekly Contest and rankings are worked out on your phone, and there is no chat. Can my child spend money? Optional purchases are coin packs, booster bundles, a Gold Season Pass and a one-time Remove Ads. Every level can be beaten without buying anything. Purchases go through the App Store or Google Play, so you can require approval for every purchase: on iPhone with Screen Time (Content & Privacy Restrictions → iTunes & App Store Purchases) or Ask to Buy, and on Android in the Play Store settings (Authentication → Require authentication for purchases) or with Google Family Link. What data does the game collect? The game does not ask for an account, your name, your email, your contacts or your location. Two analytics services (GameAnalytics and Google Analytics for Firebase) and one ad service (Google AdMob) receive some device and game information, as the privacy policy explains. Full details: iPhone privacy policy and Android privacy policy . Is it easy enough for young children? The controls are: one finger, no reading needed to play. Later levels and the timer can be hard for young children.

## How long is a level, and is it good for short breaks?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-long-is-a-level/

A level of Gobbly.io takes about 1 to 3 minutes. Early levels are short and later levels get longer. That makes it a good fit for short breaks, commutes and waiting rooms. Can I pause in the middle of a level? Yes, with the pause button at the top right. Quitting a level from the pause screen, or closing the app in the middle of a level, counts as giving up and costs one heart. How do hearts work? You have 5 hearts. Losing a level costs one heart, and one heart comes back every 30 minutes. You can also refill them with coins, or watch a short video for one heart. Winning never costs a heart, so you can keep playing as long as you keep winning. Do I lose progress if I stop? No. Your level, coins and rewards are kept. Your progress is saved on your phone automatically. On Android it is also saved in the cloud with Google Play Games, so it comes back on a new phone signed in to the same Google account. On iPhone there is no cloud save yet, so deleting the app deletes your progress. Remove Ads comes back on any phone with Restore Purchases. Is it good for the commute? Yes: one-finger controls work while you hold the phone in one hand. Yes. Every level works without Wi-Fi or mobile data. Ads, purchases and cloud saving need the internet.

No. Every level can be beaten without boosters or purchases. Boosters make a tight level easier, and you also earn them as rewards for playing. What can you buy? Optional purchases are coin packs, booster bundles, a Gold Season Pass and a one-time Remove Ads. Every level can be beaten without buying anything. Prices are shown in the game in your own currency before you buy. How do ads work in the game? There are optional reward videos you can choose to watch for extras such as more time, a heart or coins. Reward videos you choose to watch stay available. More details: how to remove ads . Why is the game free? Gobbly.io is made by a small independent developer, Sultan of Niyyat. Ads and optional purchases pay for development and updates, so anyone can play without paying up front.

## How do you remove ads in Gobbly.io?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-to-remove-ads/

Tap REMOVE ADS on the ad break screen. It is a one-time purchase that switches off the ads between levels and when you open the game, for good. Buying anything else in the game switches them off too. Reward videos you choose to watch stay available. What ads are there? There are optional reward videos you can choose to watch for extras such as more time, a heart or coins. From level 4, a short full-screen ad can also appear now and then between levels and when you come back to the game. I paid to remove ads but still see them. What do I do? Make sure you are signed in to the same Apple ID or Google account you used to buy. Open the game's Settings and tap Restore purchases . Close the game fully and open it again. Still not working? Email sultanofniyyat@gmail.com with the date of the purchase (on Android, the order number that starts with GPA.) and we will sort it out. Are the reward videos optional? Yes. Videos that give a reward, such as more time or a heart, only play when you tap to watch them. I saw an inappropriate ad. How do I report it? Ads come from Google's ad network, not from us, but we can block ad categories and advertisers. Email sultanofniyyat@gmail.com with what the ad showed and, if you can, a screenshot.

## Can you play Gobbly.io offline?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/can-you-play-offline/

Yes. Every level works without Wi-Fi or mobile data. Ads, purchases and cloud saving need the internet. What needs an internet connection? Reward videos and other ads. Buying anything, and restoring a purchase. Cloud saving with Google Play Games on Android. Does it work in airplane mode? Yes. Levels, boosters, hearts and rewards all work in airplane mode. How much mobile data does it use? Very little while you play, because the game is already on your phone. The download is about 90 MB, so install it over Wi-Fi if your data plan is small.

## Is Gobbly.io multiplayer?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-multiplayer/

No. Gobbly.io is a single-player game. There are no other balls in a level and no live opponents. The Weekly Contest and rankings are worked out on your phone, and there is no chat. Why is it called Gobbly.io then? The ".io" is a nod to the family of eat-and-grow games it belongs to. The game itself is played in single-player levels, with a goal list and a clock instead of opponents. How do the Weekly Contest and rankings work? They give you scores to beat and prizes for playing well. They are worked out on your phone and nothing about you is shown to other people. Can I play with friends? Not in the same level. Many players compare how far they have got.

## Will Gobbly.io run on my phone?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/will-it-run-on-my-phone/

Gobbly.io runs on iPhone with iOS 15 or newer and on phones with Android 7.0 or newer. The download is about 90 MB. If the store shows the game for your phone, your phone is supported. Is it on iPhone? Yes: Gobbly.io on the App Store . It is made for iPhone. Does it run on older phones? Yes. The game adjusts its graphics to the phone: phones with less memory get simpler shadows so the game stays smooth. If it still feels slow, close other apps, turn off battery saver and restart the phone. Does it drain the battery? Like any 3D game, it uses more battery than reading. Short levels help, and lowering screen brightness saves the most. Where is the safe place to download it? Only from the official stores: App Store and Google Play . Copies on APK websites, "mod" and "unlimited coins" versions are not made by us and can contain malware.

## Will I lose my progress in Gobbly.io?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/saving-progress/

Your progress is saved on your phone automatically. On Android it is also saved in the cloud with Google Play Games, so it comes back on a new phone signed in to the same Google account. On iPhone there is no cloud save yet, so deleting the app deletes your progress. Remove Ads comes back on any phone with Restore Purchases. Is progress saved automatically? Yes. You never need to press save. What happens if I update the game? Updates keep your progress. Always update from the App Store or Google Play. How do I move my progress to a new phone? On Android, sign in to Google Play Games with the same Google account on the new phone and your progress comes back. On iPhone this is not possible yet. On both, Remove Ads comes back with Restore purchases in the game's Settings. My progress disappeared. What can I do? Check that the game was not deleted and that the phone's storage was not cleared. On Android, check you are signed in to the same Google Play Games account. If something still looks wrong, email sultanofniyyat@gmail.com with your phone model and what happened.

## What is an io game?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/what-is-an-io-game/

An io game is a simple, fast arcade game where many players share one arena, usually trying to grow bigger or survive longest, with very short rounds and one-touch controls. The name comes from Agar.io (2015), a browser game that used the .io web address ending; later games copied the name and the style. Where does the name ".io" come from? ".io" is a website address ending, like .com. Agar.io used it in 2015, became a huge hit, and many games that followed (Slither.io, Diep.io, Paper.io, Hole.io) used the same ending. Over time ".io" became a sign for this family of simple grow-and-survive games. What are the main kinds of io game? Kind What you do Eat and grow Eat things to get bigger (Agar.io, Hole.io) Snake Eat to grow a longer body and trap others (Slither.io) Territory Claim area by drawing loops (Paper.io) Battle Upgrade and shoot in an arena (Diep.io) Is Gobbly.io an io game? It shares the eat-and-grow idea and the one-finger controls, but it is played in single-player levels with a goal list and a timer, not in a shared arena. Gobbly.io is a single-player game. There are no other balls in a level and no live opponents. The Weekly Contest and rankings are worked out on your phone, and there is no chat.

## What are the best games where you eat things and grow?

URL: https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/games-like-it/

The best-known eat-and-grow games are Katamari Damacy (roll a sticky ball that grows), Hole.io (a hole that swallows a city), Donut County (a story game about a growing hole) and Agar.io (cells that eat to grow). Gobbly.io mixes the rolling ball idea with short timed levels and a goal list. Which eat-and-grow games are worth knowing? Game What it is Katamari Damacy (2004) The original rolling-ball game from Namco. Roll a sticky ball that picks up everything it touches. Console and PC. Agar.io (2015) A browser and mobile game where you are a cell eating pellets and smaller players. Started the io style. Hole.io (2018) A mobile game where you are a hole in a city, racing other holes in short timed rounds. Donut County (2018) A story-driven game where you play a growing hole. Mobile, console and PC. Gobbly.io A rolling ball that eats food and toys in short timed levels with a goal list, boosters and events. Free on iPhone and Android. Which one should I pick? A story and a finished adventure: Donut County or Katamari Damacy. Racing other players: Hole.io or Agar.io. Short levels with a clear goal on your phone, alone and offline: Gobbly.io. Is Gobbly.io connected to these games? No. They are made by other companies, and their names belong to their owners. They are listed because they are the games people mean when they ask for "games where you eat things and grow".
